title: Astraeus clinical onramp — integration & safety scratchbook
content:
Context / customer summary:
- Astraeus (regional clinical workflow vendor) wants an LLM-powered triage assistant integrated into their nurse intake flow for urgent care clinics. Aim: summarize patient complaint, suggest triage level, and surface likely next steps (labs, imaging, refer).
- Must be auditable, deterministic fallback to rules for high-risk decisions, and operate inside customer VPC. EHR vendor: Epic (FHIR + bulk export via API), some clinics still send HL7 v2 messages.

Key non-negotiables mentioned on call:
- PHI must never leave Astraeus network (they insisted on Private deployment or hosted Private control plane + on-prem inference).
- Immutable audit trail for every assistant suggestion: prompt, model version, tokens, confidence scores, and final clinician action.
- Data residency: EU sites must store logs in EU.
- SLA: 95th percentile latency <= 600ms for single-turn suggestions (target for triage speed).
- Safety: automatic hard-stop / escalation path if model returns any recommendation with wording matching high-risk triggers ("admit", "intubate", "immediate ER").

Technical notes / gotchas from call:
- Expected load: 40 clinics during pilot, peak 7 concurrent inference requests per clinic -> planning for 300 concurrent small requests. Requests are short (average 60 tokens in prompt, 40 tokens output).
- Multi-turn: nurses sometimes send follow-ups referencing previous context. Need KV cache per session; retention policy 30m of inactivity.
- FHIR bundles can be large. We should design a preprocessor that extracts salient fields (age, vitals, chief complaint, meds, allergies) and attach as structured context to the prompt. Avoid token-bloat.
- EHR connectivity: two clinics use SFTP batch export of daily notes — need an offline ingestion path for retrospective audit checks.
- Logging level: they want token-level cost visibility + per-request redaction (PII fields masked). Need to confirm what mask rules cover (SSN, MRN, full DOB).
- KMS: Astraeus uses HashiCorp Vault + HSM for signing. Private deployment must integrate with their Vault cluster.

Model / quality considerations:
- They asked for a small open LLM variant that we can quantize for cost (e.g., 7B family) but also a higher-quality fallback (34B) for complex cases. Need to explain tradeoffs: throughput vs hallucination risk.
- Calibration: plan to run an eval on 5k historical triage notes to compute precision/recall on high-risk signals. Build prompt templates and an eval harness.
- Quality monitoring: tie regression alerts to prompt sets (we have Redwood Optimize hooks). Request: weekly summary emails for top 10 regressions.

Operational design sketch (rough):
1) Private control plane + on-prem inference node in Astraeus VPC (initially 2x A10G equiv, autoscale to 6).
2) Preprocessor microservice (container) that accepts FHIR/HL7, extracts canonical context, redacts PII, and calls inference runtime with structured context.
3) Inference runtime config: KV-cache per-session (ttl 30m), batch size small (2–4) to hit latency SLO. Model variants pinned per route with automatic fallback to smaller model on overload.
4) Audit streamer: write event to customer S3 (or local object store), write hashes to control plane for visibility. Provide per-request artifact id for clinician UI to inspect.

Open questions / items to confirm with customer:
- Do they want Redwood-hosted private control plane or fully air-gapped on-prem? (affects deployment timeline + legal).
- Exact redaction list (ask security team to provide a template).
- Regulatory: are these suggestions considered "clinical decision support" under local regs (may need clinician-facing disclaimers / logging retention policies >7 years?).
- Throughput headroom: pilot concurrency numbers look small, but if they roll out to 200 clinics we need to revisit commit and Dedicated capacity.

Prompting examples (quick prototypes we suggested on call):
- System: "You are a triage assistant. Use only the patient data given and clinical rules. If uncertain, say 'refer to clinician'. Flag high-risk triggers clearly."
- User prompt (after preprocessor): "age: 67, temp: 101 F, hr: 110, o2: 91%; chief complaint: shortness of breath and cough x2 days; meds: lisinopril. Known allergy: penicillin. Recent chest x-ray: none. Recommend triage level and next steps with short rationale. Return JSON: {triage_level, immediate_actions, suggested_orders, confidence_score}"
- We discussed returning structured JSON to avoid free-text hallucinations; also will implement schema validation on the control plane.

Risk mitigation patterns we proposed:
- Hard rule overlay: any model suggestion that contains an "admit"/"intubation" token triggers synchronous rules engine and clinician confirmation before UI shows to nurse.
- Conservative defaults: if confidence < 0.4 or missing vitals, default suggestion = "Clinician review required".
- Prompt engineering: explicitly instruct model to not invent labs/imaging not present in data.

Immediate next steps (who/when):
- Maya: Draft Confluence design doc capturing deployment options + audit schema — due 2026-03-10.
- Evan: Spin up eval harness and start a dry-run on 1k historical notes we have access to (anonymized) — due 2026-03-18. Link results to JIRA-ONRAMP-1123.
- Sofia: Security checklist — confirm redaction list, KMS integration patterns, and compliance asks (SOC2 / HIPAA) — due 2026-03-08.
- Sales: propose pilot commercial terms (3-month pilot, up to 50 clinics, support hours) — coordinate with legal.
- Dr. Naveen: Provide sample triage rubric and 25 annotated cases for early tuning.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments:
- Could use prefix caching for template prompts to reduce token overhead. If vitals map to common patterns, precompute small feature vector and use as structured input.
- Consider a lightweight docstore to keep per-session summaries for 30 days for audit-only queries. Ensure it’s in VPC and encrypted.
- FHIR canonicalization will be a pain — build a small staging transformer that normalizes LOINC codes we care about.

Meeting follow-up items to include in email to customer:
- Two deployment options (Private managed control plane vs On-prem blades) with pros/cons + rough TTM (4–8 weeks vs 10–14 weeks).
- Short checklist: connectivity (FHIR/HL7/SFTP), KMS access, sample de-identified dataset for eval, list of clinics for pilot, regulatory owner contact.

Unresolved / escalate to eng/security:
- Validation of 95th %ile 600ms with A10G equiv and implied batch/concurrency — need microbench numbers from serving-runtime team. (ES-req: latency microbench for 7B/34B with KV cache toggles).
- How to stream redacted token-level logs without exporting PHI — likely we send hashes + token metadata. Security to confirm acceptable pattern.

End-state sketches (for long-term):
- 99% of routine triage handled with assistant suggestions; clinicians still sign-off for any moderate/high acuity.
- Integrated quality loop: periodic sampling of model outputs vs clinician final decision; automatic retraining (or prompt re-tuning) if drift detected.

Quick glossary for Astraeus stakeholders in doc:
- KV cache: keeps prior turn tokens in efficient store to speed multi-turn inference.
- Private control plane: Redwood-managed control plane but no PHI stored, inference runs in customer VPC.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs for predictable throughput and SLA guarantees.

--raw capture end--
